chunks: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father from Banan b. Muhammad b. Isa from his father from Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

There is no servant who wakes up fasting and is then insulted, who responds: 'Indeed, I am fasting. Peace be upon you,' except that the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'My servant sought refuge from My servant by fasting. Save him from My Fire and admit him into My Paradise.'

key_terms.أجيروه: Save him/protect him (ajiruhu): an imperative from Allah to the angels to grant divine protection
key_terms.استجار: Sought refuge/protection (istajara): to seek sanctuary or shield from something
key_terms.صائم: A fasting person (sa'im): one who abstains from food, drink, and other acts from dawn to sunset

ai.seo_question: What should a fasting person say when insulted according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s) teaches that if a fasting person is insulted and responds with patience by declaring his fast and offering peace instead of retaliation, Allah Himself speaks on behalf of that servant, commanding the angels to protect him from Hellfire and admit him into Paradise. This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir (as) in the assembly of Rajab 368 AH, presents fasting not merely as abstaining from food but as a spiritual shield that transforms provocations into divine intercession.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far b. Jami` al-Himyari narrated to us from his father from Banan b. Muhammad b. `Isa from his father from `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

There is not a worshiper who is insulted while he is fasting who responds: “Surely, I am fasting. Peace be unto you” except that the Lord says: “My servant sought refuge from My servant by fasting. Save him from My Fire and bring him into My Paradise.”
